title.value: Dream to Adapt: Meta Reinforcement Learning by Latent Context Imagination and MDP Imagination

abstract.value: Meta reinforcement learning (Meta RL) has been amply explored to quickly learn an unseen task by transferring previously learned knowledge from similar tasks. However, even though Meta RL shows the ability to generalize, most state-of-the-art algorithms require the meta-training tasks to have a dense coverage on the task distribution and a great amount of data for each of them. In this paper, we propose MetaDreamer, a context-based Meta RL algorithm that requires less real training tasks and data by doing meta-imagination and MDP-imagination. We perform meta-imagination by interpolating on the learned latent context space with disentangled properties, as well as MDP-imagination through the generative world model where physical knowledge is added to plain VAE networks. Our autonomous highway merging experiments in the paper, OpenAI Gym-based and MuJoCo-based experiments show that MetaDreamer outperforms existing approaches on unseen interpolated tasks.

primary_area.value: transfer learning, meta learning, and lifelong learning
